Career and Leadership Coach

# Make your next move with clarity.

Whether you're stepping up to manage, leading through change or working out your next move, I'll help you make it well.

[Book a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation) [See the packages](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/)

Thirty years leading people at Meta, LinkedIn and Microsoft.

Is this you?

## Wherever you are in your career, there's a next move.

If one of these sounds like you, our first conversation is the quickest way to find out how coaching can help.

- You are [managing people for the first time](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/new-manager/), or about to.

- You are [leading people through a reorganisation](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/leading-through-change/) or restructuring.

- You lead a team or a business, and you have a decision to make with [nobody neutral to think it through with](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/leading-through-change/).

- You have just been promoted or [started a new role](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/new-role/).

- You want your career to move forward, but you are not sure yet [what the next step is](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/next-role/).

- You have been [laid off](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/laid-off/), or you are ready to leave, and you are deciding what comes next.

Prices and payment

## Why my prices are on the page

Most coaches at this level don't publish prices. I do, for three reasons.

You should be able to decide whether coaching is worth it before you talk to me, not after. A price on the page lets you weigh it up in your own time and come to the first conversation already knowing it fits. That makes the conversation about you, not about money.

One price list, whoever pays. If your employer funds the coaching, they pay what you would. There is no corporate rate, because the work is the same. The one exception is for people who have finished a programme with me, who continue at a lower session rate.

These are opening rates. I'm building a new practice and I'd rather work with more people at a fair price than fewer at a premium one. I'll review them in January 2027, and any change applies to new engagements only. Whatever you start at, you finish at.

How you pay.

- Our first conversation is free.

- Other packages are payable when you book. If you would rather pay by bank transfer, say so and I'll send an invoice instead.

- The Next Move can be paid in two instalments and The Leadership Engagement in three, each a dated invoice.

If you need to move a session, give me at least 48 hours notice and you can reschedule without charge. More in the [FAQ](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/faq/#fees).

Title: The Clarity Session, €350 | Matt Rutherford Coaching, Dublin

[All packages](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/)

# The Clarity Session

One decision, one situation, worked through properly in a single sitting.

€350 opening offer

Length

One 90 minute session and a 30 minute follow-up

Payment

Payable when you book.

If you continue

The fee is credited against The Next Move or The Leadership Engagement within 30 days.

[Book the Clarity Session](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/clarity) [Not sure? Start with a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

## Who it is for

Some things do not need a programme. You have an offer to weigh, a conversation to prepare for, a restructure to respond to, or a choice you keep putting off. The Clarity Session gives it 90 minutes of undivided attention with someone who has no stake in what you decide.

## What is included

- A short written brief from you beforehand

- One 90 minute session

- A written summary with the decision, options and next steps

- A 30 minute follow-up call three weeks later

## How it works

### Before

You send a short written brief: the decision or situation, what you have already considered, and what a good outcome would look like.

### The session

90 minutes, online, working through it in depth.

### After

I send a written summary with the decision, the options and your next steps.

### Three weeks later

A 30 minute follow-up call to see what has moved.

## If you want to keep going

The fee is credited against The Next Move or The Leadership Engagement if you continue within 30 days.

## Questions people ask

### What happens in a Clarity Session?

You send a short written brief beforehand, then we spend 90 minutes online working through the decision or situation. Afterwards I send a written summary with the decision, the options and your next steps, and we have a 30 minute follow-up call three weeks later.

### What kind of decision is it good for?

One with a clear question at its centre: an offer to weigh, a conversation to prepare for, a restructure to respond to, or a choice you keep putting off. If the question is bigger than one decision, such as what you want from the next few years, [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/) is usually the better fit.

### Can one session really help?

For a single, well-defined decision, yes. Much of the value comes from the brief you write beforehand and from having someone with no stake in the outcome test your thinking. The follow-up call is there to check the decision held.

### What if I want to keep going afterwards?

The fee is credited against The Next Move or The Leadership Engagement if you continue within 30 days, so you do not pay for the same ground twice.

Not sure yet?

## Start with a free conversation

It is 30 minutes and online. We talk about where you are and what you want to change, and work out together which package fits. It is a conversation, not a sales call.

[Book a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

Want something to bring? Try the [Values Finder](https://thevaluesfinder.com) beforehand.

Title: The Next Move: Career Transition Coaching | Matt Rutherford

[All packages](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/)

# The Next Move

For people making a specific career move: stepping up into management, landing the next role, or starting well in a new one.

€1,200 for the programme: €200 a session, or two payments of €600

Length

Six 60 minute sessions over twelve weeks

Payment

Payable when you book. One payment, or two of €600.

[Start with a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

## Who it is for

People about to manage for the first time, new and recent managers, and experienced professionals between roles. You have a specific move to make, and you want to make it well rather than just get through it.

## What is included

Six 60 minute sessions over twelve weeks, and:

- A transition map of your situation, built in the first session

- A workbook between sessions

- Messaging access between sessions

- A written 90 day plan you leave with

## Three tracks

In the first session we build your transition map. Then we choose the track together.

### Stepping up

Your first management role, from before you start through your first year, including your first 90 days. New to managing? Read [how to start well](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/new-manager/).

### Landing the next role

Your story, your CV and LinkedIn, interviews, and the offer. Looking by choice? Read [finding your next role](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/next-role/). Just been laid off? Read [what to do this week](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/laid-off/).

### Starting well

You have been promoted, moved sideways, or joined a new employer. Read [how to use your first 90 days](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/new-role/).

## Paying

€1,200, or two payments of €600. Payable when you book; if you would rather pay by bank transfer, say so and I will send an invoice instead. Each instalment is a dated invoice.

When the programme ends, you can continue with [Ongoing Partnership](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/ongoing-partnership/) at an alumni rate of €160 a session.

## For employers

The Next Move is also available to employers in two forms: as new-manager coaching for learning and development teams, and as individual outplacement support for someone leaving the organisation. The price is the same.

[Coaching for organisations](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/)

## Questions people ask

### Which track is right for me?

We decide together in the first session, once we have built your transition map. As a rough guide: Stepping up if you are about to manage or in your first year, Landing the next role if you are looking, and Starting well if you have just started something new.

### What happens between sessions?

You work through the workbook, and you can message me when something comes up, such as an interview, a difficult conversation or an offer. Each session picks up from where the map and the workbook have taken you.

### Is The Next Move right for me if I'm between roles?

Yes. The Landing the next role track is built for that: your story, your CV and LinkedIn, interviews and the offer. If you have just been laid off, the first conversation is a good place to work out whether now is the right time to start.

### Can my employer pay for it?

Yes, at the same price. Employers use The Next Move as new-manager coaching and as individual outplacement support. There is more on the [For organisations](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/) page.

The first step

It is a conversation, not a sales call. If I am not the right coach for what you need, I will say so and point you to someone who is.

### Conversation

30 minutes, online

We talk about where you are and what you want to change.

### Proposal

In writing

A short written proposal: the package, what we will work on, dates and price.

Title: The Leadership Engagement | Matt Rutherford Coaching

[All packages](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/)

# The Leadership Engagement

For experienced managers and senior leaders growing into a bigger role or leading through change.

€3,000 for six months: eight sessions, or three payments of €1,000

Length

Eight 90 minute sessions over six months

Payment

Payable when you book. One payment, or three of €1,000.

[Start with a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

## Who it is for

You already lead people. The role has grown, or is about to, or you are [leading through a change](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/leading-through-change/) that will test you and your team. You want a structured space to work on how you lead, over long enough for it to show.

## What is included

Eight 90 minute sessions over six months, fortnightly at first and then monthly, and:

- Structured 360 feedback gathered at the start from your manager, peers and team

- A written mid-point review

- Messaging access between sessions

- A written close-out

## How it runs

### The start

I gather structured feedback from your manager, peers and team, so the map of your situation is built on more than your own view. We use it to set what the six months are for.

### The middle

Fortnightly sessions while there is most to work on, then monthly. At the mid-point I write a short review of progress against what we set out to do.

### The close

A written close-out: what changed, what is next, and what to keep doing.

## Paying

€3,000, or three payments of €1,000. Payable when you book; if you would rather pay by bank transfer, say so and I will send an invoice instead. Each instalment is a dated invoice.

When the programme ends, you can continue with [Ongoing Partnership](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/ongoing-partnership/) at an alumni rate of €160 a session.

## For employers

If your employer is paying, we start with a three-way agreement with your sponsor, and agree the objectives up front. The sponsor gets progress against those objectives, not the content of our sessions. The price is the same, and I can send a proposal on request.

[Coaching for organisations](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/)

## Questions people ask

### Who is The Leadership Engagement for?

Experienced managers and senior leaders whose role has grown, or who are leading through a change. You already lead people, and you want to work on how you do it over long enough for the change to show.

### How does the 360 feedback work?

At the start I gather structured feedback from your manager, peers and team, and you agree who is asked. I share it with you summarised and anonymised, so no comment can be traced to the person who made it, and we use it to set what the six months are for.

### Why six months?

Because changing how you lead takes repetition. Fortnightly sessions at the start give us room to work on the hard things, and monthly sessions later let you practise in between and bring back what happened.

### Is it confidential if my employer pays?

Yes. Your sponsor gets progress against the objectives we agree together in a three-way conversation at the start, and the mid-point review as agreed. They do not get the content of our sessions or of the feedback.

The first step

### Conversation

We talk about where you are and what you want to change.

In writing

A short written proposal: the package, what we will work on, dates and price.

### Start

We agree the dates and begin.

# Ongoing Partnership

For people who want a standing thinking partner, or who want to start with a session or two before committing to a programme.

€200 per session

Length

60 minute sessions, booked singly or in blocks

Payment

Payable when you book, singly or as a block.

[Book a session](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/coaching) [For a block, start with a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

## Who it is for

Some people want a regular, neutral place to think out loud about their work, with no fixed programme. Others want to try a session or two before they commit to anything longer. Ongoing Partnership works for both.

## What is included

- 60 minute sessions, booked singly or in blocks

- A block of four for €720, saving 10%, or eight for €1,360, saving 15%

- Blocks are valid for six months and include messaging between sessions and priority scheduling

## Paying

Single sessions and blocks are payable when you book; if you would rather pay by bank transfer, say so and I will send an invoice instead.

If you have completed [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/) or [The Leadership Engagement](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/leadership-engagement/), you continue at an alumni rate: blocks of four for €640 or eight for €1,280, which is €160 a session. It is the same work with someone who already knows your map.

## Sessions or a programme?

Six single sessions cost the same as [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/), which also includes the transition map, the workbook and a written 90 day plan. If you have a specific move in mind, the programme is usually the better choice. We can talk it through in the first conversation.

## Questions people ask

### How often are sessions?

As often as suits you. Some people book every two weeks, others once a month or when something comes up. Blocks are valid for six months, so you can set your own pace.

### Should I book a block or single sessions?

Single sessions suit you if you want to try coaching, or only need to think something through now and then. A block of four saves 10% and a block of eight saves 15%, and both include messaging between sessions and priority scheduling.

### What can we talk about?

Whatever is on your mind at work: a decision, a difficult relationship, a change you are leading, or where your career is going. There is no fixed programme; you bring the agenda.

### When is a programme the better choice?

When you have a specific move to make. Six single sessions cost the same as [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/), which also includes the transition map, the workbook and a written 90 day plan.

URL: https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/laid-off/
Title: Just been laid off? What to do next | Matt Rutherford

After a layoff

# Just been laid off? Here's what to do this week, and what can wait.

Being laid off is a shock, and it is survivable. Most of what you're feeling right now, from anger to numbness to the odd flash of relief, is normal, and you don't need to decide anything today. I was made redundant myself in 2026, so this isn't theory.

By [Matt Rutherford](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/about/), Career and Leadership Coach · Updated 7 October 2026

## The first 72 hours

- Don't sign anything today. Whatever you've been handed can wait until you've read it properly and slept on it.

- Get everything in writing. If something was said in the meeting, ask for it in an email.

- Note the dates. Your notice period, your last day and when your final payment lands. Put them somewhere you'll see them.

- Decide who needs to know, and tell them on your terms. The people closest to you first. Everyone else can wait until you know what you want to say.

- Take one day off the problem. Not to pretend it hasn't happened, but because you'll think more clearly afterwards.

## The first two weeks

- Read the package properly before you sign. If any figure, date or clause is unclear, get it checked by someone qualified to check it.

- Ask for a written reference now. People are at their most generous in the first few weeks, and a few lines in writing now saves chasing later.

- Line up two or three people who will say good things about you. Ask them now, tell them what you're aiming for, and keep them posted.

- Money first, job search second. Work out your runway: what's coming in, what's going out, and how many months that gives you. Know that number before you apply for anything.

- Decide what you'll say, and keep it to two lines. Something like: "My role was made redundant in a restructure. I'm taking a few weeks to work out the right next move."

## What you're entitled to

What you're owed depends on where you work and what your contract says, so I won't try to summarise it here. The official sources are clear and kept up to date: [Citizens Information](https://www.citizensinformation.ie/en/employment/unemployment-and-redundancy/redundancy/) for Ireland and [GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/redundant-your-rights) for the UK. Anywhere else, start with your national employment authority.

## What not to do

- Fire off applications in week one.

- Take the first thing offered out of panic.

- Disappear from your network.

- Rewrite your CV before you know what you want.

- Treat this as a verdict on you. It was a decision about a role.

## When you're ready for more than a checklist

This page is the short version, enough to get you through this week. [The Layoff Field Guide](https://www.mattrutherford.co.uk/the-layoff-field-guide/) is the full version, written for exactly this situation, and it takes each of these steps further when you have the head space for it.

## When a conversation helps

Our first conversation is free: 30 minutes, online, and not a sales call. You tell me where things stand and we work out what would help most. If what you need is a recruiter, a solicitor or a rest, I'll say so.

[Book a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

When you are ready to look forward, the Landing the next role track is redundancy coaching built for this, whether you were caught in a round of tech layoffs or a quiet restructure. Online, or in person in Dublin.

### [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/): Landing the next role

Six sessions over twelve weeks.

Your story, your CV and LinkedIn, interviews and the offer, and a written 90 day plan.

€1,200 for the programme: €200 a session, or two payments of €600.

[If your company is offering outplacement support, I can be that support.](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/)

[If you are looking by choice rather than after a layoff, there is a page for that.](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/next-role/)

## Questions people ask

### Should I sign the severance agreement straight away?

No. Read it, take the time you are given, and get it checked if anything is unclear. Signing quickly rarely gets you anything you would not get by signing next week.

### How long does it take to find a job after being laid off?

It depends on your field, your level and the market, so be wary of anyone who gives you a single number. What shortens it is knowing what you are looking for before you start, and using your network rather than only job boards. Plan your money for longer than you expect.

### What do I say on LinkedIn?

Nothing, until you are ready. When you are, a short, factual post works: your role was made redundant, what you are proud of, and what you are looking for next. You do not owe anyone the full story.

### Should I tell people I was laid off?

Yes, when you are ready, and in your own words. Being laid off is common and says very little about you, and a lot of good roles come through someone who knew you were looking. Keep it to your two lines and move on to what you want next.

### Is it worth getting a coach after redundancy?

Not always. If you know what you want and the market wants it, a good CV and your network may be enough. A career coach after redundancy is worth it when you are not sure what comes next, you have not looked for a job in years, or you want someone outside the situation to think it through with.

### Can my employer pay for outplacement coaching?

Often, yes. Some employers include outplacement support in a redundancy package, and others will fund it if you ask, ideally before you sign. There is more on the [For organisations](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/) page.

### What if I don't want to go back to the same kind of job?

That is common, and worth taking seriously rather than acting on straight away. Give yourself time to work out what you actually want before you apply for anything different. It is exactly the kind of question we can work through together.

The [Values Finder](https://thevaluesfinder.com) is a 15 minute exercise if you want to work out what you actually want before you start applying.

Title: New Manager Coaching, Dublin | Matt Rutherford Coaching

Stepping up to manage

# Managing people for the first time? Here's how to start well.

Being good at the work is why you got the job, and it is not what the job is now. The first year as a manager sets habits that last, so it is worth starting deliberately. Nobody is born knowing how to run a one-to-one.

By [Matt Rutherford](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/about/), Career and Leadership Coach · Updated 7 October 2026

## Your first 90 days

Stepping up to manager is a change of job, not a bigger version of the old one. Use your first 90 days as a manager to learn the team before you try to improve it.

- Meet everyone one to one before you change anything. Ask what is working, what is not, and what they need from you. Listen more than you talk.

- Find out what your manager actually expects from you. Ask what success looks like at six months, and get it in writing if you can, even if that is your own email summing up the conversation.

- Decide what you will stop doing yourself. Write the list. Hand over anything someone in the team could do, with care, and then leave it alone.

- Set a weekly rhythm. A regular one-to-one with each person, a short team check-in, and an hour a week to think about the team rather than the work.

- Pick one thing to be known for. Clear priorities, quick decisions, honest feedback: choose one, and be consistent about it before you add a second.

## The things nobody tells you

- Your old peers are now your team, and it is awkward for them too. Name it early, in private, and agree how you will work together now.

- You will be slower at the work and faster at the job. It feels like going backwards. It isn't. You are measured on what the team delivers now, not on what you deliver yourself.

- Feedback is the whole job. Small, specific and often beats one big conversation twice a year, for praise as much as for problems.

- You will be managed harder, not softer. Your own manager expects more from you now, and will notice what your team does when you are not in the room.

## Where new managers come unstuck

- Doing the work instead of running it. It is the comfortable option, and it leaves the team waiting for you.

- Avoiding the difficult conversation. It does not get easier with time. It gets more expensive.

- Copying the last manager they had. Keep what worked for you, and remember your team are not you.

- Waiting to feel ready. Most managers feel ready some time after they needed to be. Act anyway, and adjust as you go.

## What not to do

- Change everything in the first month.

- Keep doing your old job as well as the new one.

- Stay everyone's friend at the cost of being clear.

- Save your feedback for the annual review.

- Pretend you have it all worked out.

## When a conversation helps

Our first conversation is free: 30 minutes, online, and not a sales call. Tell me about the team, the role and what is on your mind, and we will work out what would help most. If what you need is a good management course or a few more months, I'll say so.

[Book a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

New manager coaching works best early. The Stepping up track is built around your team and your first year, online or in person in Dublin.

### [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/): Stepping up

Six 60 minute sessions over twelve weeks.

A transition map of your situation, a written 90 day plan, and messaging between sessions.

€1,200 for the programme: €200 a session, or two payments of €600.

[If your company funds coaching for new managers, this is the programme I offer them.](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/)

## Questions people ask

### How long does it take to feel like a manager?

Longer than you would like, often the best part of a year. You can do the job well long before it feels natural, so don't wait for the feeling before you act like a manager.

### Should I still do some of the hands-on work?

Some, if the team is small and it keeps you close to the work. Keep it to the parts nobody else can do, and never let it crowd out your one-to-ones. If you are doing the work because it feels more comfortable, that is the sign to stop.

### How do I manage people who used to be my peers?

Name the change early, one to one, rather than pretending nothing has happened. Be the same person in a different job: fair, consistent and clear about what you expect. Some relationships will change, and that is part of the role, not a failure.

### What should I do in my first week as a manager?

Listen. Book a one-to-one with everyone on the team, ask your manager what good looks like, and change nothing yet. The first week is for learning how the team works, not for proving you can run it.

### Is coaching worth it for a first-time manager?

It can be, because the first year sets habits that last and many new managers get very little support. Coaching gives you somewhere to think through the hard conversations before you have them. If your company runs a good management programme, start with that and decide afterwards.

### Can my employer pay for this?

Often, yes. Many organisations have a learning and development budget for new managers, and the price is the same whoever pays. There is more on the [For organisations](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/) page.

### What if I'm not sure I want to manage people at all?

That is worth knowing, and it is a common feeling in the first months. Give it long enough to tell a hard start from the wrong job. If it is the wrong job, a senior specialist route is a good career, not a step back.

The [Values Finder](https://thevaluesfinder.com) is a 15 minute exercise if you want to be clear about what matters to you before you set the tone for a team.

My newsletter, [Stuff that MattRs](https://www.mattrutherford.co.uk/newsletter/), sends one useful thing a week through your first year.

Title: New Role? Coaching for the First 90 Days | Matt Rutherford

Starting well

# New role, promotion or new employer? Here's how to start well.

The first three months set how people see you for the next three years, and most people spend them trying to look busy. There is a better use of them. You don't have to prove yourself in week one. You have to understand the place.

By [Matt Rutherford](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/about/), Career and Leadership Coach · Updated 7 October 2026

## Before you start

Starting a new job well begins before day one. Whatever the induction looks like, onboarding yourself is part of the job.

- Close the last role properly. Hand over cleanly, thank the people who helped you, and leave nothing behind that will follow you.

- Write down what you think the new job is. Then check it against what you were told in the interviews and the offer, and note the gaps to ask about.

- Rest. Even a few days between roles changes how you arrive.

## The first 30 days: listen

- Meet the people who matter. Your manager, your team, your peers, and the people who depend on your work or whose work you depend on.

- Ask the same three questions of each. What is working? What isn't? What would you do in my place? The same questions make the answers easy to compare.

- Keep a list of what everyone complains about. The patterns tell you where the real problems are, and who already cares about fixing them.

- Resist fixing anything. Unless something is on fire, note it and wait. You will fix the right things later, with more support.

## Days 30 to 90: choose

- Pick the two things that matter most, and say so. Telling people your priorities is half of delivering them.

- Agree with your manager what good looks like at 90 days. Write it down, and check in against it before the 90 days are up.

- Find the person who knows how things really get done. Every organisation has one, and they are rarely where the org chart suggests.

## What if you were promoted in place?

This is the hardest version: the same people, and a different relationship. Your old peers will watch what changes, and so will your new ones.

- What changes. Who you speak for, what you can share, and who you can let off steam with. Find a new place for that, outside the team.

- What you have to let go of. Your old work, your old seat in the team, and some of the ease you had with people. That loss is real. It is also the job.

## What not to do

- Arrive with a plan you made before you met anyone.

- Say "at my last place, we..." more than once.

- Mistake being busy for being useful.

- Wait for your manager to tell you what good looks like.

- Keep quiet when the job is not the one you were offered.

## When a conversation helps

Our first conversation is free: 30 minutes, online, and not a sales call. Tell me about the role, how you got it and what you want from the first year, and we will work out what would help. If a strong induction and a good manager are all you need, I'll say so.

[Book a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

The Starting well track is new role and promotion coaching for the first 90 days, whether you have been promoted, moved sideways or joined a new employer. Online, or in person in Dublin.

### [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/): Starting well

Six 60 minute sessions over twelve weeks.

A transition map of your situation, a written 90 day plan, and messaging between sessions.

€1,200 for the programme: €200 a session, or two payments of €600.

[Some employers fund coaching for a promotion or a new senior hire.](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/)

## Questions people ask

### What should I do in my first week in a new job?

Meet people, learn names and listen. Ask your manager how they like to work and what they want from you in the first month. Change nothing yet.

### How long should I wait before making changes?

Long enough to understand why things are the way they are: a few weeks for small things, a couple of months for anything bigger. Fix what is genuinely broken straight away. Everything else can wait until you know who it affects.

### How do I handle a promotion over my former peers?

Talk to each of them one to one, early, and say plainly that the relationship has changed. Be fair and consistent, and don't make up for the change by trying to be everyone's friend. Some people will take time to adjust, and that is normal.

### What if the job is not what I was told it would be?

Write down the differences, then raise them with your manager early and calmly, as a question about priorities rather than a complaint. Often the gap closes once it is said out loud. If it does not, you will have a clearer decision to make, and you will have it sooner.

### Is coaching worth it when starting a new role?

Often, because the first 90 days in a new role shape the next few years and you rarely get time to think them through. Coaching gives you a neutral place to test your read of the organisation. If your new employer gives you a strong onboarding and a good manager, you may not need it.

### When is the right time to start coaching, before or after I start?

Just before, or in the first few weeks. Starting before lets us plan the first 90 days; starting soon after lets us work with what you are finding. Either is better than three months in, when the patterns have set.

### Can my employer pay?

Many do, especially for a promotion or a senior hire, and the price is the same whoever pays. Ask your new manager or HR team, ideally before you start. There is more on the [For organisations](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/) page.

The [Values Finder](https://thevaluesfinder.com) is a 15 minute exercise if you want to be clear about what matters to you before you set your priorities.

Title: Leading Through Change: Coaching Leaders | Matt Rutherford

Leading through change

# Leading a team through a reorganisation, a restructure or a bigger role?

I spent years leading organisational change at Meta, most recently as Global Head of Change Management. I know what it is like to carry a reorganisation you did not design, to a team who did not ask for it. Leading through change is mostly about what you do between the announcements.

By [Matt Rutherford](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/about/), Career and Leadership Coach · Updated 7 October 2026

## What people actually need from you

- Clarity about what is decided and what is not. Say both, plainly. People cope better with "not decided yet" than with silence.

- Honesty about what you don't know. "I don't know yet, and I will tell you when I do" is a complete answer.

- Consistency. They are watching for the gap between what you say and what you do, and they will find it.

- Attention to the people staying, not only the people going. The people who stay are often the ones who quietly leave six months later.

## The order of things

When you are leading a team through a reorganisation, the sequence matters as much as the message.

- Understand the change yourself first. Ask your own leaders the questions your team will ask you, until you can answer them or know that you can't.

- Work out what it means for each person before the all-hands. Who is affected, how, and what they will want to know first.

- Say the hard thing once, plainly. Don't soften it until it means nothing.

- Then repeat the plan more often than feels necessary. By the time you are tired of saying it, most people are only starting to hear it.

## Looking after yourself

You are also going through the change, often with less information than people assume and less room to talk about it.

- Find someone neutral to think with. Not your team, and ideally not your manager.

- Separate what you can influence from what you can only carry. Put your energy into the first, and be honest with yourself about the second.

- Keep the basics. Sleep, a proper day off, and one thing each week that has nothing to do with work.

## Stepping into a bigger role

Sometimes the change is your own: a bigger scope, a new layer, a team of managers rather than a team.

- What to stop doing. The work you were known for at the last level. Your job now is the conditions for the work, not the work.

- Who to lean on. The managers who report to you, and the peers who have made this step before you.

- The first conversations to have. Your manager, on what they now expect; each direct report, on what they need from you; and the peers whose work depends on yours.

## What not to do

- Promise certainty you don't have.

- Disappear into meetings while your team waits for news.

- Announce before you understand what you are announcing.

- Treat the people who are staying as fine.

- Do it alone.

## When a conversation helps

Our first conversation is free: 30 minutes, online, and not a sales call. Tell me what is changing and where you are in it, and we will work out what would help. If what you need is an employment lawyer or a stronger HR partner, I'll say so.

[Book a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

For leaders carrying a change over months, I offer executive and leadership coaching, online and in person in Dublin, built around the change you are actually leading.

### [The Leadership Engagement](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/leadership-engagement/)

Eight 90 minute sessions over six months.

Structured 360 feedback at the start from your manager, peers and team, a written mid-point review, and messaging between sessions.

€3,000 for six months: eight sessions, or three payments of €1,000.

If you want a standing thinking partner through a change rather than a programme, [Ongoing Partnership](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/ongoing-partnership/) sessions can be booked singly or in blocks.

Most leaders doing this work have it funded by their organisation. [Here is how that works.](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/)

## Questions people ask

### How do I tell my team about a reorganisation?

In person if you can, as close to the announcement as possible, and before they hear it elsewhere. Say what is changing, what it means for them, what is not decided yet and when they will hear more. Then make time for one-to-ones, because the real questions come afterwards.

### What do I say when I don't know what is going to happen?

Say that you don't know, what you do know, and when you expect to know more. People can work with uncertainty; what they struggle with is silence or false reassurance. Keep your promise about when you will update them, even if the update is that nothing has changed.

### How do I keep the people who are staying?

Talk to them one to one, early, about what the change means for them and what you need from them. Be honest about the workload, and fix what you can. The people you most want to keep usually have other options, so don't assume they are fine because they are quiet.

### How do I lead a change I disagree with?

Make your case once, in private, to the people who decided. If the decision stands, your job is to make it work well for your team, without pretending you designed it and without undermining it. If over time you find you can't do that, that is a decision about your role, and worth taking seriously.

### What does leadership coaching involve?

Regular sessions over several months, working on how you lead in your actual situation rather than in theory. In The Leadership Engagement it starts with structured feedback from the people around you and includes a written mid-point review. You bring the decisions and the conversations, and we work through them together.

### Is the 360 feedback shared with my manager?

The feedback is gathered for you, and we agree at the start what, if anything, is shared and with whom. If your employer is paying, they get progress against the objectives we agreed together, not the content of the feedback or our sessions. Nothing is shared without you knowing first.

### Can my employer pay for leadership coaching?

Usually, yes. The price is the same whoever pays, and we start with a three-way conversation to agree the objectives. There is more on the [For organisations](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/) page.

The [Values Finder](https://thevaluesfinder.com) is a 15 minute exercise if you want to be clear about what matters to you while a lot around you is moving.

My newsletter, [Stuff that MattRs](https://www.mattrutherford.co.uk/newsletter/), sends one useful thing a week while you lead through this.

The first step

Title: Your Next Role: Career Coaching, Dublin | Matt Rutherford

Landing the next role

# Ready for your next role? Work out what it is before you start applying.

Most people start with the job boards and end up with a CV that could be anyone's. The order that works is the other way round: what you want, then your story, then the search. A job search is a project. Most people run it like a lottery.

By [Matt Rutherford](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/about/), Career and Leadership Coach · Updated 7 October 2026

If you are here after a redundancy, start with [what to do if you have just been laid off](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/laid-off/).

## Before you look

- What you want more of, and less of. Look back over the last few years and be specific: the work, the people, the pace.

- The three things the next role must have. Three, not ten. These are the ones you won't trade away.

- What you would say no to. A salary floor, a commute, a kind of culture. Decide now, while nobody is offering you anything.

- The 15 minute version. The [Values Finder](https://thevaluesfinder.com) is a quick way to put words to what matters to you before you write a word of your CV.

## Your story

- The two-line answer to "what are you looking for?" If you can't say it in two lines, nobody can help you find it.

- Your CV and LinkedIn are the same story in two formats. Write the story first, then fit each format to it, not the other way round.

- The three examples you will use in every interview. Pick three pieces of work that show what you want to be hired for next, and know them well enough to tell each in two minutes.

## The search

- Your network before the boards. Tell people your two lines, and ask each of them who else you should talk to.

- A short list of ten organisations, not a hundred applications. Learn them properly, and find someone inside each one.

- A weekly rhythm and a stopping rule. Set the hours you will put in each week, and decide in advance when you will step back and change approach if it is not working.

## Interviews and the offer

- Prepare the questions you will ask, not only the ones you will answer. Good questions show judgement, and the answers tell you whether you want the job.

- Buy a day to think. "Thank you, I'm keen. Can I come back to you by Thursday?" is a normal thing to say to an offer.

- Check before you say yes. The role, the manager, the package in writing, and the first year's priorities. Ask anything you would regret not asking.

## What not to do

- Start with the job boards.

- Send the same CV to every role.

- Apply for everything that is roughly a fit.

- Leave your network until the applications stop working.

- Accept on the call before you have seen the offer in writing.

## When a conversation helps

Our first conversation is free: 30 minutes, online, and not a sales call. Tell me where you are and what you think you want next, and we will work out what would help. If a recruiter who knows your market would serve you better, I'll say so.

[Book a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation)

I coach professionals and senior people through this, online and in person in Dublin, including when the next move is a career change.

### [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/): Landing the next role

Six 60 minute sessions over twelve weeks.

Your story, CV and LinkedIn, interviews and the offer, and a written 90 day plan.

€1,200 for the programme: €200 a session, or two payments of €600.

## Questions people ask

### How do I work out what job I want next?

Start with what you want more and less of, and the three things the next role must have. Talk to people doing jobs you think you might want, and ask what their week is actually like. The answer usually comes from those conversations, not from scrolling job ads.

### Should I update my CV or LinkedIn first?

Neither. Write your two-line story first, then update both from it so they say the same thing. If you only have time for one, do LinkedIn, because that is where people will look you up.

### How long does a job search take at a senior level?

Usually longer than at earlier stages, because there are fewer roles and more of them are filled through networks and search firms. It depends on your field and the market, so plan for months rather than weeks. A senior job search moves faster when you know exactly what you are looking for.

### Is it better to apply directly or through my network?

Through your network, where you can. A warm introduction gets you read, and often tells you about roles before they are advertised. Apply directly as well for roles that fit closely, and say who you know there if you know someone.

### How do I know if I should change career rather than role?

Ask whether you are tired of the job or tired of the work. If it is the organisation, the manager or the pace, a new role may fix it. If it is the work itself, a career change is worth exploring properly, with small tests before a big leap.

### Is a career coach worth it if I already know what I want?

Sometimes not. If you know what you want and the market wants it, a sharp CV and your network may be enough. Coaching is worth it when you want a clearer story, better interviews or a better offer, or when the search is taking longer than it should.

### How is this different from a recruiter?

A recruiter works for the employer and is paid when they fill a role, so they are looking for a match for a job they already have. I work for you, on what you want and how to get it, whichever job that turns out to be. Good recruiters are worth knowing, and I will often suggest talking to one.

If you skipped it above, the [Values Finder](https://thevaluesfinder.com) is a 15 minute exercise to work out what you actually want before you start applying.

My newsletter, [Stuff that MattRs](https://www.mattrutherford.co.uk/newsletter/), sends one useful thing a week while you run your search.

It is a conversation, not a sales call. If I am not the right coach for what you need, I will say so and point you to someone who is.

### Conversation

We talk about where you are and what you want to change.

Title: About Matt Rutherford: Career and Leadership Coach, Dublin

# Matt Rutherford

Career and Leadership Coach

I know these moves from the inside: I have made them, led people through them, and been on the receiving end of them. I coach the way I would want to be coached: direct, practical, and on your side.

30 [Years at Meta, LinkedIn and Microsoft](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mattrutherford/)

AC [Association for Coaching](https://www.associationforcoaching.com/members/?id=82268264)

2024 Coaching diploma

## Where I have been

I spent thirty years in senior roles at Meta, LinkedIn and Microsoft. Most recently, as Global Head of Change Management at Meta, I led a team of senior programme managers delivering hundreds of change projects a year around the world.

I have also been laid off twice in the last six years, so I know that side of a reorganisation too.

[See my career on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mattrutherford/)

## Why coaching

The part of that work I valued most was always the one to one conversations. A manager working out how to lead the team they used to be part of. A leader with a decision nobody else could make for them. Someone whose role had just disappeared. Good support at those moments changes what happens next, and coaching lets me give it properly.

How I work

## A map first, then a plan

In the first session we map your situation. Every session after that works a part of the map, so you leave with a written plan rather than a set of notes.

### Where you are

Your role, your strengths, and what is and is not working right now.

### Where you are going

The move you want to make, described specifically enough to plan for.

### What is in the way

The gaps, habits and circumstances that slow you down.

### Who matters

The people whose support, decisions or opinion will shape the move.

## Who I work with

People making progress in their careers, from experienced professionals to executives, in any sector, usually at one of five moments:

- [Looking for the next role](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/next-role/)

- [Managing people for the first time](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/new-manager/)

- [Starting a new role or a promotion](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/new-role/)

- [Leading through change](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/leading-through-change/)

- [Just been laid off](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/laid-off/)

## Training and standards

I hold a Diploma in Executive and Business Coaching (2024) and I am a registered member of the [Association for Coaching](https://www.associationforcoaching.com/members/?id=82268264). My coaching follows the Association for Coaching code of ethics.

## Stuff that MattRs

I also write [Stuff that MattRs](https://www.mattrutherford.co.uk/newsletter/), a weekly newsletter on ideas, growth and clarity at work.

## Where I work

I live in Dublin. Sessions are online by default, and in person by arrangement. I work with clients in Ireland, the UK and Europe.

[Book a free conversation](https://calendly.com/mattrutherfordcoaching/conversation) [See the packages](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/)

Title: FAQ: Prices, Payment, Confidentiality | Matt Rutherford

FAQ

# Questions people ask

If your question is not here, ask it in the first conversation, or [send me a message](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/#contact).

- [Getting started](#getting-started)

- [Fees and payment](#fees)

- [Working together](#working-together)

## Getting started

### What happens in the first conversation?

It is 30 minutes, online. You tell me where you are and what you want to change, and I ask questions until I understand it. By the end we will both know whether coaching would help and, if it would, which package fits.

If you want to go ahead, I send you a short written proposal afterwards: the package, what we will work on, dates and price. If you want something to bring, try the [Values Finder](https://thevaluesfinder.com) beforehand.

### Is it a sales call?

No. It is a conversation about your situation, and I will not push you to buy anything. If I am not the right coach for what you need, I will say so and point you to someone who is.

### Who do you work with?

People making progress in their careers, from experienced professionals to executives, in any sector. The usual reasons people get in touch are [looking for the next role](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/next-role/), [stepping up to manage](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/new-manager/), [starting a new role](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/new-role/), [leading through change](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/leading-through-change/), or [having just been laid off](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/laid-off/).

### Do I need to be a leader already?

No. Many of the people I work with are experienced professionals thinking about, or just starting, their first management role. [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/) is built for exactly that.

### How many sessions will I need?

It depends on what you want to change. A single decision can often be worked through in one [Clarity Session](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/clarity-session/). A specific career move usually takes the six sessions of [The Next Move](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/the-next-move/), and changing how you lead takes the eight sessions over six months of [The Leadership Engagement](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/leadership-engagement/). We work out which fits in the first conversation.

### Are sessions online or in person?

Online by default, over Google Meet. In person by arrangement: in Dublin, or further afield if travel costs are covered. I work with clients in Ireland, the UK and Europe.

## Fees and payment

### How much does career coaching cost?

Coaching prices vary widely, and many coaches don't publish theirs. Mine are on the [packages page](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/): €350 for a Clarity Session, €200 for a single session, €1,200 for The Next Move and €3,000 for The Leadership Engagement. Blocks of four or eight sessions are €720 and €1,360, and the price is the same whoever pays.

### How do I pay, and can I pay in instalments?

Our first conversation is free. Other packages are payable when you book; if you would rather pay by bank transfer, say so and I will send an invoice instead.

Yes to instalments: The Next Move can be paid in two payments of €600, and The Leadership Engagement in three payments of €1,000, each a dated invoice.

### Is there a discount for continuing after a programme?

Yes. If you have completed The Next Move or The Leadership Engagement, you can continue with [Ongoing Partnership](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/ongoing-partnership/) in blocks of four for €640 or eight for €1,280, which is €160 a session.

### Can my employer pay, and how do I ask?

Yes, and the price is the same whoever pays. Many employers have a learning and development budget, and some managers can approve coaching from a team budget. Ask your manager or your HR team. I can send you a short proposal to forward, with the objectives, the package and the price.

When an employer pays, we start with a three-way conversation to agree objectives. There is more on the [For organisations](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/for-organisations/) page.

### What is your cancellation and rescheduling policy?

If you need to move a session, give me at least 48 hours notice and you can reschedule without charge.

## Working together

### Is what we discuss confidential, including from my employer?

Yes. What we discuss stays between us. If your employer is paying, they get progress against the objectives we agreed together, not the content of our sessions, and we agree what is shared before anything is.

The only exceptions are the ones the Association for Coaching code of ethics sets out, such as a serious risk of harm to you or someone else, or a legal requirement to disclose.

### How is coaching different from therapy or mentoring?

Coaching looks forward: it works on what you want to do next and how, starting from where you are now. Therapy works on your wellbeing, often including the past, and if that is what you need I will say so and suggest you find a therapist. A mentor shares their own path; I bring experience too, but the work is built around your situation and your decisions.

### Are you accredited?

I am a registered member of the [Association for Coaching](https://www.associationforcoaching.com/members/?id=82268264) and hold a Diploma in Executive and Business Coaching (2024).

### Do you offer team coaching?

Not at the moment. I work one to one. If your organisation wants coaching for several people, I can put together a proposal for each of them individually.

Title: Coaching for Organisations | Matt Rutherford Coaching

For organisations

# Coaching for someone on your team

For HR and learning and development teams sponsoring coaching, and for managers approving it from a team budget.

[Request a proposal](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/?subject=Proposal%20request&situation=sponsor#contact)

## Who it suits

### A new manager in their first year

Someone good at the work who now has to lead the people doing it. The first year sets habits that last.

### A leader stepping up or leading through change

A bigger role, a new team, or a reorganisation to carry through, with nobody neutral to think it through with.

### Someone leaving the organisation

People leaving deserve good support. Individual outplacement coaching helps them work out what comes next and land it.

## What you can choose

### New-manager coaching

The Next Move for a manager in their first year: six sessions over twelve weeks, a transition map and a written 90 day plan. €1,200. [What a new manager can expect](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/new-manager/).

### Individual outplacement

The Next Move for someone leaving: six sessions over twelve weeks on what comes next, from their story, CV and LinkedIn to interviews and the offer. €1,200. There is also [a page you can share with them](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/laid-off/).

### Leadership coaching

[The Leadership Engagement](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/leadership-engagement/) for more senior people: six months, structured feedback at the start and a written mid-point review. €3,000. [More on leading through change](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/leading-through-change/).

## Confidentiality, plainly

You get progress against the objectives we agree together. You do not get the content of sessions. What someone says in a session stays between them and me, and everyone knows that from the start. It is what makes the coaching work.

For The Leadership Engagement, I also write a mid-point review of progress against the objectives, shared as agreed at the start.

## Cost and invoicing

The same [published prices](https://staging.mattrutherfordcoaching.com/coaching/) as for individuals: there is one price list, whoever pays. For more than one person, I will put together a single proposal.

I invoice the organisation directly, payable by bank transfer or card. If you need a purchase order number on the invoice, send it with the go-ahead and I will include it.

## Questions organisations ask

### What does outplacement coaching include?

Six one-to-one sessions over twelve weeks with The Next Move, focused on what comes next: the person's story, their CV and LinkedIn, interviews and the offer, ending with a written 90 day plan. It is confidential, and the first session is within two weeks of the go-ahead.

### How do you report progress?

Against the objectives the three of us agree at the start. You get progress against those objectives, not the content of sessions. For The Leadership Engagement I also write a mid-point review, shared as agreed at the start.

### Can you work with our purchase order process?

Yes. I invoice the organisation directly, payable by bank transfer or card. Send the purchase order number with the go-ahead and I will put it on the invoice.

### Can you coach several people in our organisation?

Yes, one to one. I don't offer team coaching, but I can put together a single proposal covering each person individually.

How it starts

## Three steps to getting started

### Proposal

In writing

Tell me about the person and what you want the coaching to achieve. I reply with a short written proposal.

### Three-way conversation

Objectives agreed

You, the person being coached and I agree the objectives and what progress looks like.

### Start

Within two weeks

Coaching begins, with the first session within two weeks.

Title: Privacy Statement | Matt Rutherford Coaching

Privacy

# Privacy statement

What I collect about you, why, how long I keep it, who else handles it, and your rights.

## Who is responsible for your data

The controller is Matt Rutherford, a sole trader trading as Matt Rutherford Coaching, based in Dublin, Ireland. You can contact me about anything in this statement at [matt@mattrutherfordcoaching.com](mailto:matt@mattrutherfordcoaching.com).

## What I collect and why

### When you use the contact form

Your name, email address, the situation you choose, your role and subject if you give them, and your message. I use them to reply to you. The form is handled by Formspree, which passes your message to my email.

### When you book a conversation or session

Your name, email address, the time you choose and any answers you give on the booking form. I use them to schedule the session and send reminders. Booking is handled by Calendly.

### When you pay

Card payments at booking are taken through Calendly by Stripe. I do not see or store your card details. For invoiced work I keep your name, billing details, the invoice and the payment record. If an employer pays, I keep the billing contact's name, email and any purchase order number.

### When we email

I keep the emails we exchange. My email is provided by Google Workspace.

### During coaching

I keep brief session notes to support our work: what we covered, what you agreed to do next, and the transition map and plans we build. They can include things you tell me about your work and life. Online sessions run on Google Meet. I never record sessions.

If you share information about your health or other sensitive matters, I record it only where it is needed for the coaching and only with your explicit consent.

### 360 feedback

For The Leadership Engagement, I gather feedback about you from people you agree with me, such as your manager, peers and team. I collect their comments, use them only for your engagement, and share them with you summarised and anonymised, so no comment can be traced to the person who made it. The people giving feedback are told how it will be used before they give it.

### If your employer sponsors the coaching

I keep the sponsor's contact details, the objectives agreed in the three-way conversation, and the progress updates and mid-point review shared with them. Sponsors do not receive the content of sessions.

### The Values Finder

The [Values Finder](https://thevaluesfinder.com) is a separate site with its own [privacy notice](https://thevaluesfinder.com/privacy.html). Your answers stay in your own browser. If you ask it to email your report, it is sent through the email service Resend and not kept afterwards. If you tick the box, it adds you to my newsletter. I only see your results if you choose to send them to me.

### The Clarity Check

[CONFIRM: draft wording for the Clarity Check] The Clarity Check runs in your browser. Anything you write in it stays there and is never sent to me. The answers you choose from the lists, and the result you are shown, are counted in my analytics with nothing that identifies you, so that I can improve the questions. If you go on to book a conversation, the booking link tells Calendly which result you saw.

### Website analytics

This site uses Umami, a privacy-focused analytics tool that I host myself, on the same server as this site in Finland. It counts page views, which pages are visited, the referring site, browser, device type and country, and a few events such as which answers are chosen in the Clarity Check. [CONFIRM: events wording] It does not use cookies and does not build a profile of you.

### Fonts and hosting

The site's fonts are loaded from Google Fonts, so your browser sends your IP address to Google when a page loads. The site is hosted by Hetzner Online on a server in Finland. The server keeps access logs (page requested, time and browser, with IP addresses anonymised) for security, for one year.

### Cookies

This site does not set cookies. Calendly sets its own cookies when you go to it to book.

## The legal basis

- Contract: booking, delivering coaching, invoicing and taking payment, and the steps before an agreement, such as the first conversation and the proposal.

- Legitimate interests: replying to enquiries, gathering 360 feedback for an engagement you have agreed to, keeping the site secure, and understanding how the site is used through cookie-free analytics.

- Legal obligation: keeping financial records for Irish tax purposes.

- Consent: the newsletter, and any sensitive information you choose to share in coaching. You can withdraw consent at any time.

## How long I keep it

- Session notes and coaching materials: 12 months after our last session, then deleted, unless we are still working together or have agreed something different.

- 360 feedback: kept with the session notes, on the same 12 month schedule.

- Enquiries that do not lead to coaching: 12 months from our last contact, then deleted.

- Invoices and payment records: six years, as Irish tax law requires.

- Booking records in Calendly: Calendly keeps past bookings until I delete them. I delete them on the same 12 month schedule.

## Who else handles your data

I do not sell your data or share it for marketing. These services process it on my behalf:

- Calendly, for booking (United States).

- Stripe, for card payments at booking, through Calendly.

- Formspree, for the contact form (United States).

- Google Workspace, for email and for Google Meet video calls.

- Google Fonts, for the website's fonts.

- Hetzner Online, for website and analytics hosting (Finland).

Some of these providers are based in the United States. Calendly and Google are certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and also use standard contractual clauses. Formspree states that it transfers data only where the law permits, and takes steps to keep it protected.

## Your rights

You have the right to:

- see the personal data I hold about you and get a copy

- have it corrected if it is wrong

- have it deleted, unless I have to keep it by law

- restrict or object to how I use it

- receive it in a portable format

- withdraw consent where I rely on it

To use any of these, email [matt@mattrutherfordcoaching.com](mailto:matt@mattrutherfordcoaching.com). I will reply within one month.

## Complaints

If you are unhappy with how I handle your data, please tell me first and I will try to put it right. You also have the right to complain to the Data Protection Commission, the supervisory authority in Ireland, at [dataprotection.ie](https://www.dataprotection.ie/).

Last updated 6 October 2026.
